recent_posts.title: Unverified leak claims Anthropic built a powerful new AI model called Claude Mythos
recent_posts.summary: A sensationalized claim about a supposed leak of 3,000 confidential files from Anthropic, allegedly revealing an unreleased AI model called 'Claude Mythos' that surpasses Opus models in coding, reasoning, and cybersecurity capabilities. The content mixes real details about Anthropic's safety-focused release practices with fabricated or unverified claims, including misspelling 'Anthropic' as 'Enthropic' throughout, and ends with a call to subscribe — indicating this is likely low-quality viral content or misinformation.

recent_posts.title: How Cursor challenged VSCode with AI native architecture
recent_posts.summary: Cursor, an AI-native code editor built by four MIT students, challenged VSCode's dominance by integrating AI into its core architecture rather than as an add-on. Unlike VSCode's extension-based approach, Cursor provides full codebase understanding, enabling features like Composer that can refactor entire modules autonomously. The 2.0 release introduced agent-first development with multi-agent systems and reinforcement learning. Despite rapid growth to 7 million users, Cursor faced challenges including Microsoft restricting marketplace access and infrastructure stability issues that drove some developers back to VSCode.

recent_posts.title: The evolution of Remix from React Router to a web standards framework
recent_posts.summary: Remix is a fullstack web framework created by the developers behind React Router (Ryan Florence and Michael Jackson). Initially launched as a paid product in 2020, it went open source in 2021 and was acquired by Shopify in 2022. The framework focuses on web standards, server-side rendering, parallel data loading, and progressive enhancement. In 2024, Remix merged with React Router v7, and in 2025, Remix 3 made a radical shift away from React to Preact, prioritizing minimal dependencies and native web APIs, though this breaking change divided the community.

recent_posts.title: How the ILOVEYOU virus infected 50 million computers and caused $15 billion in damage
recent_posts.summary: The ILOVEYOU virus, created by Filipino student Onel de Guzman in 2000, became the most destructive computer worm in history. Written in VBScript and disguised as a love letter email attachment, it infected 45-50 million computers worldwide (10% of internet-connected devices at the time), causing $5.5-15 billion in damages. The virus spread through Microsoft Outlook, deleted files, and attempted to steal dial-up passwords. It breached major institutions including the Pentagon, CIA, NASA, and British Parliament, forcing many organizations to shut down their email systems. The incident exposed gaps in cybercrime laws and demonstrated the power of social engineering attacks.

recent_posts.title: How deleting an 11 line npm package broke the internet
recent_posts.summary: In 2016, developer Azer Koçulu deleted all 350 of his npm packages after a trademark dispute over his 'kik' package, inadvertently breaking major websites and applications worldwide. The removal of his 11-line 'left-pad' package caused widespread outages at companies like Facebook, Netflix, and PayPal because thousands of projects depended on it. NPM responded by restoring the package without the author's permission and implementing new policies, including a 24-hour deletion window and restrictions on unpublishing packages with dependencies. This incident highlighted the fragility of the JavaScript ecosystem's dependency chain and led to significant changes in how package registries handle deletions and trademark disputes.

recent_posts.title: The 2018 GitHub DDoS attack that changed cybersecurity
recent_posts.summary: In 2018, GitHub faced the largest DDoS attack in cybersecurity history, reaching 1.35 terabytes per second using memcached amplification techniques. Attackers exploited misconfigured memcached servers worldwide to amplify small requests into massive responses, overwhelming GitHub's infrastructure. The company successfully defended against the attack by partnering with Akamai Prolexis for traffic scrubbing and rerouting. This incident exposed thousands of vulnerable servers globally and prompted widespread security improvements across hosting providers.

recent_posts.title: Svelte 5 Complete Course ( 2025 )
recent_posts.summary: Svelte 5 is a modern JavaScript framework that compiles components into optimized vanilla JavaScript at build time, eliminating runtime bloat. Unlike React or Vue.js which use virtual DOM, Svelte directly updates the DOM for better performance. The framework features component-based architecture, reactive state management with runes, props for data passing between components, text interpolation for dynamic content, conditional rendering, loops with each blocks, snippets for reusable markup, and side effects handling. Key concepts include state management using state runes, derived values, children props for passing HTML content, and event handling with on:click syntax.

recent_posts.title: Every Vue.js Concept Explained ( Complete Course )
recent_posts.summary: Vue.js is a versatile JavaScript framework that simplifies building modern web applications through a component-based structure, a large community, and its lightweight nature. This comprehensive course covers essential Vue.js concepts like components, reactivity, text interpolation, attribute bindings, computed properties, conditional rendering, slots, and more. The post explains the setup of a Vue.js project, folder structure, and demonstrates various functionalities with examples to help developers efficiently manage UI logic and improve front-end skills.

recent_posts.title: Understanding GraphQL basics and server setup
recent_posts.summary: GraphQL is a querying language for APIs that allows apps to request specific data, addressing issues like overfetching and underfetching prevalent in REST APIs. The post outlines the setup of a GraphQL server using Node.js and Apollo Server, focusing on type definitions, resolvers, relationships, and mutations for handling data effectively.

recent_posts.title: Mastering advanced web animations with Motion.dev
recent_posts.summary: Motion.dev is an advanced animation library for modern web projects using JavaScript, React, or Vue. It simplifies the creation of complex animations, providing extensive control over transformations and transitions. Installation is easy through npm, and it integrates seamlessly with frameworks like React and Next.js. Key components include the motion object, which leverages initial, animate, and exit props to manage animations effectively.
